subject: Arts

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT considered an element of design?
questions.explain: Balance is a Principle of Design (a way of organizing elements), not a basic Element of Design. Line, Texture, and Shape are all fundamental elements.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Which element of art is formally defined as a continuous mark made on a surface by a moving point?
questions.explain: A line is the most basic element of design, created when a point moves across a surface, leaving a continuous mark.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Different types of lines convey different psychological feelings. What kind of emotion or feeling does a strictly horizontal line usually suggest?
questions.explain: Horizontal lines parallel the horizon and remind us of a person sleeping or the calm surface of a lake, which generally communicates rest, peacefulness, and stability.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: When a line curves around to connect with its starting point and enclose a space, a two-dimensional area is created. What element of design is this?
questions.explain: A shape is a two-dimensional, flat, enclosed area. It is defined whenever a line connects to enclose a space.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Shapes that are mathematically precise and regular, such as squares, circles, and triangles, are known as:
questions.explain: Geometric shapes are precise, mathematically defined shapes often created using tools like rulers and compasses. They include circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an 'organic shape'?
options: A perfect rectangle drawn with a ruler
A free-form silhouette of a fallen leaf
questions.explain: Organic (or biomorphic) shapes are irregular, free-flowing, and not mathematically perfect. They often resemble things found in nature, like leaves, clouds, or animals.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: While 'shape' is two-dimensional, which element of design refers to objects that are three-dimensional, having length, width, and depth?
questions.explain: Form refers to a three-dimensional object (like a sculpture or a cube) that has length, width, and depth (thickness).
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: If a circle is considered a 2D shape, what would be its corresponding 3D 'form'?
questions.explain: A sphere is the three-dimensional equivalent (form) of a two-dimensional flat circle (shape).
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: The element of art that refers to the surface quality or 'feel' of an object—whether it is smooth, rough, soft, or hard—is called:
questions.explain: Texture relates to how the surface of a material feels to the touch or how it looks like it would feel if touched.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: When an artist draws the bark of a tree on a flat piece of paper so realistically that it looks rough, but the paper still feels perfectly smooth to the touch, this is an example of:
questions.explain: Visual or implied texture is created using drawing techniques to trick the eye into perceiving a surface quality (like roughness) on a surface that is actually flat and smooth.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Which element of design refers to the relative lightness or darkness of a colour, helping to create highlights and deep shadows in an artwork?
questions.explain: Value, also known as Tone, describes how light or dark a given colour or hue is. It is crucial for creating the illusion of three-dimensional form on a flat surface through shading.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: The area around, above, below, or within objects in a piece of artwork is known as:
questions.explain: Space is the element of art that defines the area around and between objects, as well as the illusion of depth in a 2D artwork.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts
